questions.text: Analyse the role played by India in the liberation of Bangladesh.
questions.text_as_printed: Analyse the role played by India in the liberation of Bangladesh. (Difficult )

answer.value:
Role of India in the Liberation of Bangladesh
Bangladesh was formerly a part of Pakistan and was known as East Pakistan.
From 1960 onwards, the people of East Pakistan struggled for a separate nation under the leadership of Sheikh Mujibur Rahman and his party, the Awami League.
Due to large-scale human rights violations in East Pakistan, India's military intervention became necessary.
In the decisive war of 1971, West Pakistan was defeated, and East Pakistan emerged as the independent nation of Bangladesh.

questions.text: What were the effects of the 1962 Sino–Indian War?
questions.text_as_printed: What were the effects of the 1962 Sino–Indian War? (Average )

answer.value:
Effects of the 1962 Sino–Indian War
In 1962, against the backdrop of the Tibet issue, China launched a major attack on India from the North-East Frontier to Ladakh (Jammu and Kashmir).
China later declared a unilateral ceasefire, but by then it had occupied about 14,671 square miles of Indian territory.
The war deeply disappointed Jawaharlal Nehru, one of the architects of the Panchsheel Principles.
The Line of Actual Control (LAC) continues to serve as the de facto border between India and China.
China continues to retain control over Aksai Chin (Eastern Ladakh), covering approximately 14,671 square miles of Indian territory.
